title: Vicky Kaushal Has Blocked 18 Months for One Film. Mahavatar Might Be the Biggest Bet in Bollywood.
excerpt: A six-month physical transformation, a year-long shoot, Shraddha Kapoor in talks, and a Christmas 2026 exit — Amar Kaushik's mythological epic with Vicky as Parashurama is playing for keeps.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Vicky Kaushal commits 18 months exclusively to the film 'Mahavatar'.
  • The film features a year-long shoot starting January 2027.
  • Shraddha Kapoor is in talks for the female lead role.
  • Mahavatar aims for a 2028 release, moving from Christmas 2026.
  • The film seeks to create a cinematic universe around Indian mythology.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=mQfD0TNloko There is a photo doing the rounds from earlier this week — **Vicky Kaushal** leaving the **Maddock Films** office in Juhu, dressed in a white linen shirt and dark cargo pants, cap pulled low, sunglasses on. It looks casual. It is anything but. Because behind that office door, one of the most ambitious projects in Hindi cinema history is quietly taking shape. And Vicky Kaushal has decided to give it everything. ## Eighteen Months. One Role. According to a Pinkvilla exclusive, Vicky has committed to an extraordinary **18-month window** exclusively for **Mahavatar** — the mythological epic directed by **Amar Kaushik** (the man behind *Stree*, *Bhediya*, and *Bala*). The commitment began in June 2026 with a six-month intensive prep schedule: physical transformation, bulking up, and a series of acting workshops designed specifically for the role. > "Amar has designed a very detailed prep module for Vicky. It's not just about the physicality, but also about getting into the psychological and emotional graph of the character." — Source close to the production The film is slated to go on floors in **January 2027** and will shoot for an entire year, wrapping by December 2027. During this period, Vicky plans to take on **zero other projects** — a nearly unheard-of commitment in an industry where stars routinely juggle three or four films simultaneously. > **"He wants to be fully invested, which is why he has consciously decided not to take up any other assignments during the shoot." This is not Method acting for a press tour."** > "Vicky is treating Mahavatar as a once-in-a-lifetime project. He wants to be fully invested, which is why he has consciously decided not to take up any other assignments during the shoot." This is not Method acting for a press tour. This is a man betting his prime years on a single vision. ## The Parashurama of It All Vicky will play **Parashurama** — the warrior-sage avatar of Vishnu, a figure who occupies a fascinatingly violent corner of Hindu mythology. He is not the gentle deity. He is the one who took up the axe. The one who wiped out the Kshatriya race twenty-one times over. He is rage with divine permission. ![Maddock Films — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/6/6e/Maddock_Films_logo.jpeg) For Amar Kaushik, who has built his career on genre films that speak to the Indian heartland, Mahavatar represents a seismic leap — from the streets of Chanderi to the mythological battlefields. Maddock Films, the production house behind the entire horror-comedy universe, is mounting this as its most ambitious production to date. ## Christmas Is Off. The Scale Is On. In a significant development, **Mahavatar has officially vacated the Christmas 2026 release slot**. The move is directly tied to Vicky's scheduling — he is still wrapping **Love & War**, the Sanjay Leela Bhansali epic co-starring **Ranbir Kapoor** and **Alia Bhatt**, which releases **January 21, 2027**. There was simply no way to have Mahavatar ready for December. The exit from Christmas means the film is now likely targeting a **2028 theatrical window** — giving it the extended post-production time that a VFX-heavy mythological spectacle demands.

## Shraddha Kapoor: The Missing Piece? Here is where it gets interesting. According to a Mid-Day report, **Shraddha Kapoor** has been approached to play the female lead opposite Vicky. > "Shraddha fits the brief perfectly. The team was keen on someone who brings star value and presence. Plus, the Vicky-Shraddha pairing will be fresh, and the makers are confident this combination will resonate with the audience." If she comes on board, it would be Shraddha's fifth project with Maddock Films and her first on-screen pairing with Vicky. She is already the face of the *Stree* franchise and is headlining the upcoming *Eetha* for the same banner. The synergy is obvious — Kaushik knows her, Maddock trusts her, and the audience adores her. Before Shraddha, **Deepika Padukone** was reportedly in consideration for the role. The production team was looking for "someone who can bring gravitas and emotional depth to the role written opposite Parashurama." Both names tell you everything about the scale Maddock is chasing. ## Why the Diaspora Should Care Mahavatar is not just another mythological retelling. It is an attempt to build the kind of cinematic universe around Indian mythology that Marvel built around comic books — except rooted in stories that billions of people already know intimately.
Casting Insights
›Shraddha Kapoor approached for female lead.
›Potential fifth project with Maddock Films.
›Deepika Padukone was also considered.
For the Indian diaspora, projects like this represent a specific kind of cultural moment: seeing your mythology rendered with the production value, the seriousness, and the scale that Hollywood has always afforded to Greek and Norse myths. It matters. And with Vicky's physical commitment, Kaushik's storytelling instincts, and Maddock's track record of turning genre bets into blockbusters, Mahavatar has every ingredient to be the film that finally gets it right. The axe has been picked up. Now we wait for the swing.
